title: The Ledger of Port Mahon
premise: In 1798, on the Mediterranean island of Menorca, Tamsin Kavanagh works in her father's print shop in Port Mahon, cutting type and believing the island's wars belong to other people. When British forces requisition the town and seize every ledger of names, debts, and allegiances, Tamsin discovers her father has been secretly printing pamphlets for a Spanish sympathizer, Mateu Ferragut — the man she secretly loves and who is now declared an enemy combatant. Bound by a promise made in peacetime to warn him before the armistice is signed (or sabotaged), she must navigate occupation, betrayal by her own brother, and the machinery of military bureaucracy that reduces people to ledger entries. In the end, Tamsin chooses truth over loyalty to the crown, forging a false armistice page that saves Mateu and the town's accused, though it costs her father's shop, her brother's life, and her own invisibility forever.
about_author: Isandro Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing naval correspondence from the Mediterranean garrisons. The Ledger of Port Mahon is his second novel, drawn from a misfiled requisition order he found in 2009.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Tamsin Kavanagh's POV. She cuts type in her father's print shop above the harbor, invisible among the apprentices who think she's a boy. Establishes her craft, her father's quiet radicalism, and her belief that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: contentment built on illusion.

chapters.title: Mateu at the Water Stair
chapters.summary: Tamsin meets Mateu Ferragut, a Spanish clerk who brings manuscripts to print under false imprints. Their flirtation happens over proofs and margins. POV alternates with Mateu's brief section revealing he knows more than he says. Beat: first love disguised as business.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: During the town festival, Mateu asks Tamsin for one promise: if war comes, warn him before any list of names reaches the governor. She laughs it off but agrees. Her brother Aldous watches from the crowd. Beat: an oath made lightly that will weigh everything.

chapters.title: Ships on the Horizon
chapters.summary: British sails appear off the harbor. The town's merchants calculate; the poor bar their doors. Tamsin's father burns nothing and hides everything. Beat: dread arriving slowly, like weather.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: The army occupies Port Mahon and seizes all ledgers, records, and presses. A young officer, Captain Voss, catalogs the Kavanagh press but spares it — suspiciously. Tamsin realizes names are now currency. Beat: the ordinary world confiscated.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin glimpses the master ledger: every resident sorted into loyal, suspect, enemy. Mateu's name appears under 'enemy at large.' Her promise becomes concrete and dangerous. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Aldous Enlists
chapters.summary: Her brother Aldous takes a commission with the occupiers, believing collaboration will protect the family. Father and son quarrel; Tamsin stands between them. Beat: family fracturing along the fault line of duty.

chapters.title: What the Press Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin finds hidden plates in the cellar: pamphlets her father printed for the resistance, bearing Mateu's handwriting. She understands her childhood was never neutral. Beat: disillusionment and strange pride.

chapters.title: Captain Voss Calls Again
chapters.summary: Voss visits under pretense of inspecting type quality. He is intelligent, lonely, and possibly fishing. Tamsin performs innocence while measuring him. Beat: cat-and-mouse with stakes she can't yet name.

chapters.title: The Empty Room Above the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Tamsin searches for Mateu through the occupied town, following a chalk mark only printers would know. She finds his abandoned lodgings and a half-burned letter addressed to her. Beat: longing braided with urgency.

chapters.title: Aldous Knows
chapters.summary: Aldous confronts Tamsin: he saw her at the chandlery. He offers silence in exchange for her silence about their father's plates. Beat: blackmail inside love, loyalty curdling.

chapters.title: The Governor's Armistice Draft
chapters.summary: Through Voss's careless talk, Tamsin learns an armistice is being negotiated — and that its signing requires a final purge list of 'enemy elements' to be executed beforehand. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Father and daughter secretly reprint a decoy pamphlet to draw suspicion away from the real network. Tamsin's skill with type becomes a weapon. Beat: competence as empowerment.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Someone betrays the network; two printers are arrested. Tamsin recognizes the forged handbill that lured them — set in type she herself cut. Beat: guilt as a physical wound.

chapters.title: Mateu Returns
chapters.summary: Mateu appears at the shop after dark, gaunt and hunted. He came not for himself but to destroy the ledger copy naming his cousins. Tamsin must tell him about the purge list. Beat: reunion shadowed by countdown.

chapters.title: Three Days Before Signing
chapters.summary: They plan: steal or alter the ledger before the armistice ceremony. Aldous, assigned to guard the records office, is the obstacle and the key. Beat: hope requiring betrayal.

chapters.title: Dinner with Captain Voss
chapters.summary: Voss invites Tamsin to dine, probing her loyalties with courtesy. She lies beautifully and hates how well he listens. Beat: temptation of a simpler path — safety through complicity.

chapters.title: The Brother's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin begs Aldous to look away during the theft. He refuses — then privately copies the purge list himself, torn between crown and blood. Beat: Aldous revealed as tragic, not villainous.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Case
chapters.summary: Tamsin smuggles blank ledger pages into the records office inside a type case. Nearly caught by a sentry, saved by a drunk officer's interruption. Beat: terror and exhilaration.

chapters.title: Forgery
chapters.summary: She alters the purge list overnight using matched type, striking four names including Mateu's cousins. Her hands shake; her father steadies them. Beat: sin committed for love, described without excuse.

chapters.title: Discovery of a Mismatched Kern
chapters.summary: A meticulous clerk notices inconsistent letterforms. Voss begins an audit of every press in town. Beat: the noose tightening by inches.

chapters.title: Aldous Confesses
chapters.summary: Aldous, unable to live the lie, tells Voss someone altered the list — withholding that it was Tamsin. He is arrested for obstruction. Beat: sacrifice that damns him twice.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Tamsin is questioned. Voss shows her the kern evidence and gives her one night to confess. She reads in his eyes that he wants her innocent. Beat: intimacy as interrogation.

chapters.title: The Night Decision
chapters.summary: Alone, Tamsin weighs confession against flight. Her father offers to take the blame; she refuses. She decides to finish what she started: forge the armistice itself. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Stealing the Signature Page
chapters.summary: Using knowledge of the print trade and Voss's distracted grief over Aldous, Tamsin accesses the treaty draft. Beat: audacity at maximum risk.

chapters.title: What the Treaty Actually Says
chapters.summary: Reading the full document, she learns the armistice is a trap: terms guarantee amnesty publicly while a sealed annex orders executions regardless. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Tamsin and her father reprint the annex and distribute it anonymously across the garrison, forcing officers to confront what they signed. Mutinous murmurs begin. Beat: truth as ordnance.

chapters.title: Voss Understands
chapters.summary: Voss traces the forgery to Tamsin at last. Instead of arresting her, he burns the evidence — because the annex shamed him too. Beat: unexpected mercy from the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Signing Ceremony
chapters.summary: The armistice is signed before a hostile crowd that has read the annex. The executions are quietly cancelled; the governor saves face. Beat: victory that feels like held breath.

chapters.title: Aldous's Cell
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits Aldous before his transport to prison. They forgive each other without absolution. He tells her to stop hiding. Beat: grief and grace.

chapters.title: Mateu's Choice
chapters.summary: Amnestied, Mateu is offered passage home to Palma — and asks Tamsin to come. She cannot leave her father and the wrecked shop. Beat: love against duty, both honored, neither won.

chapters.title: The Farewell at the Mole
chapters.summary: Mateu sails. Tamsin keeps the promise fully kept and the love fully lost. He leaves her the chalk mark and a printed line: 'Set me again someday.' Beat: heartbreak with dignity.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Press
chapters.summary: The requisitioned shop is returned gutted. Father and daughter sort melted type together, mourning the trade and the town's innocence. Beat: desolation before rebuilding.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin begins her own book: not names for authorities, but testimonies of the occupation, collected door to door. Beat: identity forged from loss.

chapters.title: Voss Departs
chapters.summary: Voss, reassigned, leaves her a gift: Aldous's confiscated notebook and a single word of apology. Tamsin understands enemies are made, not born. Beat: complicated gratitude.

chapters.title: Aldous Comes Home
chapters.summary: Two years later, pardoned and diminished, Aldous returns. He asks to learn the trade. Tamsin hands him a composing stick. Beat: reconciliation without forgetting.

chapters.title: The Testimony Printed
chapters.summary: The testimony book is published under no imprint at all — truly anonymous, truly hers. It circulates beyond Menorca. Beat: invisibility transformed into power.

chapters.title: Letter from Palma
chapters.summary: A letter arrives in Mateu's hand: he has opened a small press. No request, only news, and the same printed line. Tamsin smiles at the open question of it. Beat: hope without resolution.

chapters.title: Set Me Again
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Tamsin's POV. Years on, she trains apprentices — girls included — in the shop rebuilt beside the old one. History, she now knows, happens here, to everyone, and someone must set the record straight. Beat: earned peace, identity complete.
